# Conformance cases

Written by `tests/conformance/generate.py`; do not edit.

## NetFlow v5

| Case | Covers | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header_and_record_layout` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format"; Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Flow Record Format" | One datagram with one record. Every header and record field holds a different value, so each must be read from its own offset and width. |
| `count_30_records` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format", "count" (1-30) | The largest datagram the format allows: 30 records, 1464 bytes. |
| `count_zero` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format", "count" | A header announcing no records is a packet without flows. The format documents a count of 1 to 30, so Wireshark calls this one malformed. |
| `field_ranges` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format"; Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Flow Record Format" | One record with every field at its highest value and one with every field zero: all integers are unsigned and none is truncated. The pad bytes of the first record are non-zero and must not leak into a field. |
| `sampling_interval` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format", "sampling_interval" | The 16-bit sampling field: the first two bits are the mode, the remaining 14 the interval. Four datagrams: 0/0, 1/1, 2/1024 and 3/16383. |
| `several_exporters` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format" | Datagrams from three exporters, one of them over IPv6, and two engines of one exporter: v5 is stateless, so each datagram is read on its own, in capture order. |
| `truncated` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format"; Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Flow Record Format" (robustness) | A datagram shorter than its header, one whose second record is cut short, and one of exactly 23 bytes are discarded; the whole datagram between them is read. |
| `other_versions` | Cisco NetFlow Export Datagram Format, "Version 5 Header Format", "version" | Datagrams laid out as v5 but announcing versions 0, 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11 and 0x0500 are not v5 and are discarded; the v5 datagram after them is read. |

## NetFlow v9

| Case | Covers | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s11_examples` | RFC 3954 section 11 (11.1 to 11.5) | The export packet of the RFC's examples: a Template FlowSet (template 256), a Data FlowSet of three flow records, an Options Template FlowSet (template 257, scoped by line card, with two padding bytes) and a Data FlowSet of two options records. Count is 7. |
| `s5_1_header` | RFC 3954 section 5.1 | The packet header, each field a different value: version, count, sysUpTime, UNIX secs, sequence number and source ID. Three packets from two source IDs, with sequence numbers that are not consecutive: the header is reported as sent. |
| `s5_2_template_flowset` | RFC 3954 section 5.2 | Template FlowSets: one holding two template records (256 and 257), a second in the same packet holding a third with the highest template ID (65535) and a single one-byte field. Data of each template follows, in the same packet and in the next. |
| `s5_3_data_flowset_padding` | RFC 3954 section 5.3 | Data FlowSets padded to a 4-byte boundary. Records of 5 bytes: one record and 3 padding bytes, two and 2, three and 1, four and none. Records of 7 bytes: one record and 1 padding byte. The Length covers the padding, the padding is shorter than a record, and it must not be read as one. Two Data FlowSets of one template in a packet are two sets. |
| `s6_1_options_template_flowset` | RFC 3954 section 6.1 | Options Template FlowSets. Option Scope Length and Option Length are in bytes, not fields. One template scoped by all five scope types (System, Interface, Line Card, Cache, Template), in a FlowSet with two padding bytes; two more templates in one FlowSet, the second with strings. |
| `s6_2_options_data_record` | RFC 3954 section 6.2 | Options data records: scope values first, then the option values, in template order. Scope fields of 1, 2 and 4 bytes; a FlowSet of three records, and one of a single record with padding. |
| `s7_template_refresh_and_redefinition` | RFC 3954 sections 7 and 9 | Template 256 is sent, used, sent again unchanged (a refresh) and used again; then it is sent with a new definition, which must override the old one at once (section 9): the data that follows, in the same packet and the next, is read by the new definition. |
| `s7_template_id_scope` | RFC 3954 sections 7 and 9 | Template IDs are unique per exporter and per observation domain (source ID). Template 256 means one thing in source ID 1 of exporter 192.0.2.1, another in its source ID 2, and a third from exporter 192.0.2.2; data of each is read by its own definition. Source ID 3 never sent a template 256, so its data stays undecoded. |
| `s8_field_types` | RFC 3954 section 8 | Field types at the lengths section 8 gives them, and at the other lengths it allows where the length is N: counters (IN_BYTES, IN_PKTS, FLOWS) of 4 and of 8 bytes, interfaces of 2 and of 4, AS numbers of 2 and of 4, a 3-byte IPv6 flow label, a 3-byte MPLS label, MAC addresses, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and names padded with NULs to the field's length. |
| `s8_unknown_field_types` | RFC 3954 section 8 | Field types the collector has no definition for (40001, and 32769, whose top bit means nothing in v9) keep their bytes and their length, so the fields after them are still read at the right offset. |
| `s9_data_before_template` | RFC 3954 section 9 | Data and options data arrive before their templates, which the collector must not assume to be in the same packet. A packet is printed as it was read, so the first two keep their FlowSets undecoded, as sent; once the templates arrive, data of the same templates is decoded. |
| `s9_template_kinds_share_ids` | RFC 3954 sections 6.1 and 9 | Templates and options templates share one ID space: an options template sent with the ID of a template overrides it, and the other way around. |
| `s4_reserved_flowset_ids` | RFC 3954 sections 4 and 5.2 | FlowSet IDs 2 to 255 are reserved for FlowSets yet to be defined. A collector steps over them by their Length and reads the FlowSets around them. |
| `truncated_header` | RFC 3954 section 5.1 (robustness) | Datagrams cut inside the 20-byte header (19, 10 and 2 bytes) are discarded; the whole packet after them is read. |
| `truncated_flowset` | RFC 3954 sections 5.2 and 5.3 (robustness) | A FlowSet whose Length runs past the end of the datagram, and one whose Length (3) is shorter than its own header. RFC 3954 does not say what a collector does; rustflow discards the whole packet, the FlowSets before the broken one included, and reads the packets around it. |

## IPFIX

| Case | Covers | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `appendix_a_examples` | RFC 7011 appendix A.1 to A.4 | The appendix's examples, value for value. The first message is the one A.1 describes, 152 octets: the Template Set of A.2.1, the Data Set of A.3, the Options Template Set of A.4.1 (two padding octets) and a Data Set of two options records. The second carries the enterprise-specific examples: the Template Set of A.2.2, the Options Template Sets of A.4.2 and A.4.3, the Data Set of A.4.4 and data of the other two templates. The enterprise-specific elements are unknown to the collector and keep their octets. |
| `appendix_a_5_variable_length` | RFC 7011 appendix A.5 | A.5.1: a 5-octet value after a one-octet length. A.5.2: a 1000-octet value after the three-octet length 255, 1000. |
| `s3_1_message_header` | RFC 7011 section 3.1 | The message header, each field a different value: version, Length, Export Time, Sequence Number and Observation Domain ID. Then a message of every field at its highest, and one that is a header alone (Length 16). |
| `s3_2_field_specifier` | RFC 7011 section 3.2 | Field specifiers with and without the enterprise bit. With it, four more octets carry the enterprise number and the element belongs to that enterprise: element 8 of enterprise 32473 is not IANA's sourceIPv4Address. Enterprise numbers 1 and 4294967295, and the highest element ID, 32767, in both spaces. The elements the collector has no definition of keep their octets, and the fields after them are read at the right offset. |
| `s3_3_1_set_padding` | RFC 7011 sections 3.3.1 and 9 | Sets padded to 4-octet and 8-octet boundaries; the padding is shorter than any record of the Set and is not read as one. Data records of 5 octets with 3, 2 and 1 padding octets, of 7 with 1, of 9 with 7 (an 8-octet boundary), and an Options Template Set with 2. One Data Set is padded with non-zero octets, which does not make the message malformed (section 9.1). |
| `s3_3_2_set_ids` | RFC 7011 section 3.3.2 | Set IDs: 2 is a Template Set, 3 an Options Template Set, 256 and above a Data Set. 0 and 1 are not used and 4 to 255 are reserved: a collector steps over such a Set by its Length and reads the Sets around it. |
| `s3_4_1_template_record` | RFC 7011 sections 3.4.1 and 8 | Template records: two in one Template Set, a second Template Set in the same message, the highest Template ID (65535), a template of a single one-octet field, and a template holding an element more than once, whose values are reported in template order. |
| `s3_4_2_options_template_record` | RFC 7011 sections 3.4.2.1 and 3.4.2.2 | Options template records. Field Count counts the scope fields too, and the scope fields come first. One template with two scope fields, one whose fields are all scope fields, one scoped by an enterprise-specific element; two of them in one Set. |
| `s3_4_3_data_record` | RFC 7011 section 3.4.3 | Data records: field values one after another in template order, with no header of their own. A Data Set of twenty records, Data Sets of three templates in one message, and two Data Sets of one template side by side. |
| `s3_1_version_number` | RFC 7011 section 3.1; RFC 3954 section 5.1 | One exporter sends NetFlow v5, NetFlow v9 and IPFIX to one port; the Version field tells them apart. Template 256 of observation domain 0 is defined once in NetFlow v9 and once, differently, in IPFIX: the two protocols keep separate templates, and data of each is read by its own. |
| `s4_reporting_options_templates` | RFC 7011 sections 4.1 to 4.4 | The four options templates the RFC specifies and a record of each: Metering Process Statistics (4.1), Metering Process Reliability Statistics (4.2), Exporting Process Reliability Statistics (4.3) and Flow Keys (4.4). Those of 4.2 and 4.3 hold the same timestamp element twice, for the first and the last time; both values are reported, in template order. |
| `s5_timing` | RFC 7011 sections 5.1 and 5.2 | Export Time is seconds since the UNIX epoch in 32 bits, as dateTimeSeconds values are. Flow times given as microsecond offsets from the Export Time (flowStartDeltaMicroseconds and flowEndDeltaMicroseconds) are unsigned 32-bit integers, up to about 71 minutes. dateTimeSeconds at the two ends of its range: the epoch, and one second before it wraps on 7 February 2106 at 06:28:16. |
| `s6_1_data_type_encodings` | RFC 7011 sections 6.1.1 to 6.1.10 | A value of every abstract data type the IANA registry uses, at its full size: unsigned8, 16, 32 and 64, signed32 (two's complement), macAddress, ipv4Address, ipv6Address, float64 (IEEE binary64), boolean (1 true, 2 false), string (UTF-8, one with a two-octet character), octetArray, and the four dateTime types: seconds and milliseconds since the UNIX epoch, and NTP timestamps for micro- and nanoseconds. Three records: ordinary values, the highest values, and the lowest. |
| `s6_1_6_ill_formed_utf8` | RFC 7011 section 6.1.6 | String values that are not well-formed UTF-8 (a lone continuation octet, an overlong encoding, a truncated sequence): the collector should detect such values. They are not read as text but reported as their octets, in hexadecimal, and the record's other fields are kept; the record between them, with well-formed strings, is whole. |
| `s6_2_reduced_size_encoding` | RFC 7011 section 6.2 | Integers and floats sent in fewer octets than their type implies. unsigned64 elements in 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 octets; unsigned32 in 1, 2 and 3; unsigned16 in 1; signed32 in 1, 2 and 3, where the sign must be preserved; float64 as float32. Three records: the highest value of each size (the lowest for the signed ones), the highest positive signed values, and ordinary values. |
| `s7_variable_length` | RFC 7011 section 7 | Variable-length elements (field length 65535), each value carrying its own length: in one octet when below 255, or in three (255, then two octets) for any length. Three variable-length fields between two fixed ones, with values of 0, 1, 254, 255, 256 and 1100 octets, the three-octet form used for short and for empty values as well, and records of different sizes following one another in a Set. |
| `s8_template_refresh` | RFC 7011 sections 8 and 8.4 | Over UDP an exporter sends its templates again and again. A template received again unchanged is not an error and changes nothing: data before and after it is read alike. The templates are sent alone, with data, and after data in the same message. |
| `s8_1_template_withdrawal` | RFC 7011 sections 8.1 and 8.4 | Template withdrawals: of template 256, of options template 257, of all templates (Template ID 2 in a Template Set) and of all options templates (Template ID 3 in an Options Template Set). Over UDP a collector must ignore them (section 8.4), so the data after each withdrawal is still decoded by the templates sent before. |
| `s8_4_template_id_reuse` | RFC 7011 sections 8.1 and 8.4 | Over UDP an exporter reuses a Template ID by exporting a new template for it. Template 256 is sent with a new definition, and later as an options template: data that follows is read by the latest definition. |
| `s8_template_id_scope` | RFC 7011 section 8 | Template IDs are unique per Transport Session and Observation Domain. Template 256 means one thing in domain 1 of exporter 192.0.2.1, another in its domain 2, a third from exporter 192.0.2.2 and a fourth from an exporter reached over IPv6; data of each is read by its own definition. Domain 3 never sent a template 256, so its data stays undecoded. |
| `s8_data_before_template` | RFC 7011 sections 8 and 8.4 | Over UDP a template may be lost or arrive after its data. A message is printed as it was read, so the first two keep their Data Sets undecoded, as sent; once the templates arrive, data of the same templates is decoded. |
| `s9_unknown_information_elements` | RFC 7011 section 9 | Elements the collector does not understand, IANA's and enterprise-specific, of fixed and of variable length. Their identifiers are noted (printed by number) with their octets, and the elements around them are read as usual. |
| `s9_1_malformed_message_header` | RFC 7011 section 9.1 | Malformed messages, which a collector must discard: a Length (15) shorter than a message header, a Length (0), a datagram cut inside the header, a message cut short of its Length, and reserved Version values (0, 11 and 0x0a00). The well-formed message after them is read. |
| `s9_1_malformed_set_length` | RFC 7011 section 9.1 | Messages with a nonsensical Set Length: a Set longer than its enclosing message, and Sets whose Length (0 and 3) is shorter than a Set header. Each message also holds a valid Template Set and Data Set before the broken Set; the RFC has the collector discard the message, not just the broken Set, so nothing of them is reported. The well-formed message after them is read. |
| `s9_1_malformed_variable_length` | RFC 7011 section 9.1 | Messages holding a variable-length value longer than its enclosing Set: a one-octet length of 5 with 4 octets left, and a three-octet length of 1000. The Template Set and the first record of each message are valid; the RFC has the collector discard the message. The well-formed message after them is read. **Known deviation:** rustflow keeps both messages, reporting the Data Set as undecoded octets, where RFC 7011 section 9.1 has the collector discard a message with such a length. |
| `rfc6313_4_5_1_basic_list` | RFC 6313 section 4.5.1 | basicList: a semantic octet, a field specifier (with an enterprise number when its top bit is set) and the values. Lists of a fixed-length IANA element, of an enterprise-specific element, of a variable-length element, and an empty list; in a variable-length field with the one- and the three-octet length, and in a field of fixed length. Each list is reported with its values, and the fields before and after it are read. |
| `rfc6313_4_5_2_sub_template_list` | RFC 6313 section 4.5.2 | subTemplateList: a semantic octet, a Template ID and records of that template. A list of two records, an empty list, and a list of a template the collector does not have, which is reported as null. The fields before and after each list are read. |
| `rfc6313_4_5_3_sub_template_multi_list` | RFC 6313 section 4.5.3 | subTemplateMultiList: a semantic octet, then groups, each a Template ID, a length covering those four octets and the records, and records of that template. A list of two groups of different templates, and a list with no group. The fields before and after each list are read. |
| `rfc5610_3_type_information` | RFC 5610 sections 3 and 3.9 | Type records: options records scoped by informationElementId and privateEnterpriseNumber that give an element's data type, semantics and name. Eight elements of enterprise 32473 are described, among them the types the IANA registry has no element of (signed8, signed16, signed64, float32); a ninth is not. Data of a template using all nine follows: the described elements are read by their described types, the ninth keeps its octets. The elements are printed under their numbers. |

## sFlow v5

| Case | Covers | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s5_sample_datagram` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, sample_datagram_v5 and address | The datagram header, each field a different value: agent address, sub-agent ID, sequence number and uptime. An agent address of each type: IPv4, IPv6 and unknown, which carries no bytes. A datagram of no samples, and one with every integer at its highest. |
| `s5_flow_sample` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, flow_sample (format 1) | A compact flow sample, each field a different value: sequence number, source ID, sampling rate, sample pool, drops, input and output. The source ID's top byte is its type and the rest its index; an interface's top two bits are its format and the rest its value. A second sample with every field at its highest, and one of no records. |
| `s5_data_source_and_interface` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, sflow_data_source and interface | Source IDs of each type (0 an ifIndex, 1 a VLAN, 2 a physical entity) and the interface encodings the specification lists: 0x00000002 (ifIndex 2), 0x00000000 (unknown), 0x40000001 (discarded, reason 1), 0x40000102 (discarded, reason 258), 0x80000007 (sent to 7 interfaces), 0x80000000 (sent to an unknown number) and 0x3FFFFFFF (no interface: the device itself). |
| `s5_flow_sample_expanded` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, flow_sample_expanded (format 3) | Expanded flow samples, whose source ID and interfaces each take two 32-bit integers: a type and an index, a format and a value. Indexes past what the compact form holds (2^24 and 2^30), and every field at its highest. |
| `s5_counters_sample` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, counters_sample (format 2) and counters_sample_expanded (format 4) | Counters samples, compact and expanded, with a record of each standard counter structure: if_counters, ethernet_counters, tokenring_counters, vg_counters, vlan_counters and processor. Every counter holds a different value, the 64-bit ones past 32 bits. The processor's CPU percentages are signed: -1 means unknown. |
| `s5_sampled_header` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, sampled_header (format 1) and header_protocol | Sampled headers of 44, 45, 46 and 47 bytes, which XDR pads with 0, 3, 2 and 1 bytes: the header is its length, without the padding, and the record after it is read. Frame length and stripped bytes are reported as sent. Header protocols other than Ethernet: IPv4 (11), and a number the specification does not assign (99). |
| `s5_sampled_ethernet_ipv4_ipv6` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, sampled_ethernet (format 2), sampled_ipv4 (3) and sampled_ipv6 (4) | The parsed packet records: Ethernet frame data, whose MAC addresses are six bytes padded to eight, and IPv4 and IPv6 data, whose addresses are fixed-length and carry no type. Every field holds a different value. |
| `s5_extended_switch_router_gateway` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, extended_switch (format 1001), extended_router (1002) and extended_gateway (1003) | Switch, router and gateway data. A next hop of each address type: IPv4, IPv6 and unknown. Gateway data with an AS path of a sequence, a set and another sequence, with communities; one with an empty path and no communities; and one whose path holds an empty segment. |
| `s5_extended_user_url` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, extended_user (format 1004) and extended_url (1005) | User and URL data, whose strings are XDR variable-length: lengths of 0 to 9 bytes cover every amount of padding, and the field after each string is read. Users are opaque bytes with a character set (106 is UTF-8, 3 is ASCII); URLs name which end is the server. |
| `s5_unknown_formats` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, data_format, sample_record, flow_record and counter_record | Every sample and record names its format, an enterprise and a number, and carries its length, so that a receiver can step over those it does not know. A sample of an enterprise's own format, flow and counter records of an enterprise's and of unknown standard formats, and one of no bytes: each is kept as sent, under its enterprise and format, and what surrounds it is read. The highest enterprise (2^20 - 1) and format (4095) numbers. |
| `s5_several_samples_and_agents` | sFlow Version 5 section 5, sample_datagram_v5 | Datagrams of flow and counters samples together, compact and expanded, from two agents and two sub-agents of one, one agent reached over IPv6: each datagram is read on its own, its samples in order. |
| `drops_discarded_packet` | sFlow Dropped Packet Notification Structures section 2, discarded_packet (format 5), extended_egress_queue (1036), extended_acl (1037) and extended_function (1038) | Dropped-packet notifications: a sample with an expanded source ID, drops, input and output ifIndex, a reason and the records describing the packet. Reasons from the ICMP unreachable codes (0), from the sFlow codes (257 TTL exceeded, 258 ACL), and one the specification does not assign (9999), which is reported by number. The records added for drops: egress queue, ACL and function. |
| `truncated_and_other_versions` | sFlow Version 5 section 5 (robustness) | Datagrams a collector cannot read are discarded whole: cut inside the header, cut inside the second sample, announcing more samples than it holds, of another version (2, 4, 6), and with an agent address of a type the specification does not define (3). The whole datagram after them is read. |
